name: RASopathy

criteria.description: Characteristic craniofacial features including hypertelorism, ptosis, and low-set ears
Presence of congenital heart defects such as pulmonary valve stenosis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Identification of pathogenic variant in RAS-MAPK pathway genes (e.g., PTPN11, SOS1, RAF1, KRAS)
Multiple lentigines, café-au-lait spots, or keratosis pilaris
Postnatal short stature or failure to thrive

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic facial dysmorphism, cardiac anomalies, and pathogenic variant in RAS-MAPK pathway gene
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by additional features such as cutaneous manifestations and growth abnormalities.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism (hypertelorism, ptosis, low-set ears)
searchTerms: distinct facial features like wide-set eyes, droopy eyelids, low ears
unusual face shape with hypertelorism and ptosis
narrowing of pulmonary heart valve from birth
birth defect causing pulmonary valve stenosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pathogenic variants in RAS-MAPK pathway genes
searchTerms: genetic mutations causing RAS-MAPK pathway disorders
gene changes affecting cell growth signaling
RAS-MAPK pathway gene variants causing developmental symptoms
many lentigines or pigmented skin patches
skin pigmentation abnormalities with many spots

common.symptomName: Developmental delay or mild intellectual disability
searchTerms: delayed development or mild learning difficulties

occasional.symptomName: Hearing loss due to sensorineural impairment
searchTerms: hearing loss due to nerve damage
difficulty hearing from inner ear problems

occasional.symptomName: Ocular abnormalities including strabismus and refractive errors
searchTerms: eye problems including crossed eyes and vision errors
ocular abnormalities like misaligned eyes and refractive issues
renal swelling due to urine buildup

laboratory: Elevated levels of natriuretic peptides in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
imaging: Echocardiography showing pulmonary valve stenosis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
MRI or ultrasound for lymphatic abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic variants in PTPN11, SOS1, RAF1, KRAS, NRAS, BRAF, or other RAS-MAPK pathway genes
other: Characteristic facial features on clinical examination
Skin examination revealing lentigines or café-au-lait spots

distinguishingFeatures: Overlapping features but Noonan syndrome is a specific RASopathy subtype with distinct gene mutations
More prominent cardiac defects and facial features
Presence of neurofibromas and optic gliomas
More extensive café-au-lait spots and Lisch nodules

redFlags: Severe hypertrophic cardiomyopathy causing heart failure
Recurrent unexplained lymphedema or respiratory distress
references: Tartaglia M, Gelb BD. Disorders of dysregulated signal traffic through the RAS-MAPK pathway: phenotypic spectrum and molecular mechanisms. Annu Rev Genomics Hum Genet. 2005;6: 39-68.
Rauen KA. The RASopathies. Annu Rev Genomics Hum Genet. 2013;14:355-69.
